value.overview:
Brownfield change to the layered FastAPI/SQLAlchemy URL shortener to get it ready for the campaign (Q-1: about 50 RPS, redirect p95 < 100 ms, one instance; Q-2: hardened SQLite, no new driver). The change is additive and low-risk.

(1) SQLite hardening and pool settings in app/core/db.py:
- A connect listener runs the literal PRAGMAs journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL, only for file-based SQLite.
- The busy timeout is set through the sqlite3 connect_args 'timeout'.
- QueuePool size, overflow and timeout come from four new validated settings.
- In-memory SQLite gets no pool kwargs and no WAL.

(2) Startup schema upgrade in a new app/core/schema.py. It runs in the lifespan after create_all, is idempotent, and adds the only schema change: the nullable links.expires_at column (literal ALTER TABLE). If the upgrade fails, startup fails.

(3) Startup log lines. One structured line reports the effective DB tuning and one reports the schema-upgrade outcome. Neither contains the URL or any secrets.

(4) Redirect hot path:
- One narrow SELECT (id, url, is_active, expires_at) into a RedirectTarget dataclass.
- One shared private service helper checks deactivation first, then expiry (now >= expires_at, using an injectable clock).
- The read transaction ends before the click INSERT.
- The click is still recorded synchronously and best-effort; a failure logs one WARNING without the IP.
- Errors on the redirect path (404/410) carry Cache-Control: no-store.
- Expired links return 410 {"detail": "Link has expired"}.

(5) Expiry API:
- POST /api/links accepts an optional expires_at; the idempotency hash covers it only when it is present, so old keys still replay.
- New PATCH /api/links/{code} sets or clears expires_at.
- Create and detail responses return expires_at; detail also returns is_expired.

(6) Analytics:
- Daily stats are aggregated in SQL with GROUP BY and dialect-guarded day expressions. The response contract is unchanged.
- New GET /api/links/{code}/stats/hourly returns zero-filled UTC-hour buckets over [start, end), capped at 744 hours, aggregated in SQL with dialect-guarded hour expressions that use no bound parameters.

(7) Probes: explicit HEAD routes for /healthz and /readyz, outside the OpenAPI schema, so HEAD probes no longer fall through to the catch-all.

(8) MySQL: binary collation on links.code through a String.with_variant that applies only to mysql/mariadb.

(9) Docs: README, API, OPERATIONS (WAL, backups, locking, the upgrade, a campaign runbook and the PostgreSQL scaling path) and CHANGELOG are corrected.

All other contracts are unchanged: the 307 with exact Location and no-store, the 410 on deactivation, the error JSON, the auth on /api/links*, the daily stats schema, and the layering rules. requirements.txt is unchanged.

components.name: Settings (core/config)
components.responsibility:
Validated env settings. Adds:
- SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS: int, 0..60000, default 5000
- DB_POOL_SIZE: int ≥1, default 5
- DB_MAX_OVERFLOW: int ≥0, default 10
- DB_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: float >0 and ≤300, default 30.0

Existing fields and defaults are unchanged. There is no module-level instance.

components.name: DB engine and tuning (core/db)
components.responsibility: create_db_engine with per-dialect pooling, the SQLite connect listener (literal WAL/synchronous PRAGMAs), the busy timeout via connect_args, log_engine_tuning() for the startup line, the session factory and get_db.

components.name: Startup schema upgrade (core/schema)
components.responsibility: ensure_links_expires_at(engine): inspects the links columns and runs a literal, dialect-guarded ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN expires_at only when the column is missing. Logs the outcome and re-raises on failure.

components.name: Errors and logging (core)
components.responsibility: Adds InvalidInputError (422) and the LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL constant. JsonFormatter emits the new structured extra fields used by the tuning and schema log lines.

components.name: ORM models
components.responsibility: Link gains the nullable expires_at DateTime column. links.code gets a MySQL/MariaDB-only utf8mb4_bin collation through with_variant. base.py gains to_naive_utc().

components.name: Repositories
components.responsibility: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target (the narrow 4-column SELECT returning a RedirectTarget). ClickRepository.daily_counts and hourly_counts (SQL GROUP BY with dialect-guarded bucket expressions), plus module-level statement builders that tests can compile without a connection. created_at_since is removed.

components.name: Schemas
components.responsibility: LinkCreate.expires_at (optional, normalised to naive UTC). expires_at on LinkCreatedResponse, and expires_at plus is_expired on LinkDetailResponse. New LinkExpiryUpdate (PATCH body, extra=forbid), HourlyClicks and LinkHourlyStatsResponse. LinkStatsResponse is unchanged.

components.name: LinkService
components.responsibility: Injectable clock. Shared _resolve_target/_check_redirectable used by GET and HEAD (deactivation, then expiry). Best-effort click recording after the read transaction ends. create_link with expires_at and the backward-compatible idempotency hash. set_expiry for PATCH. is_expired in the detail.

components.name: StatsService
components.responsibility: get_stats via SQL day aggregation, with unchanged semantics. get_hourly_clicks: range parsing and alignment, validation, SQL hour aggregation and zero-filling.

components.name: Health router
components.responsibility: GET and HEAD /healthz (never touch the DB) and GET and HEAD /readyz (SELECT 1). The HEAD routes are excluded from the schema and return empty bodies.

components.name: Links router
components.responsibility: POST create (expires_at), GET detail, PATCH expiry, DELETE, GET daily stats, GET hourly stats. All require the API key.

components.name: Redirect router
components.responsibility: Catch-all GET and HEAD /{code}, registered last. Raw 307 with exact Location and no-store. 404/410 JSON with Cache-Control: no-store. OpenAPI documents the expired 410.

components.name: App factory
components.responsibility: create_app passes the pool and SQLite settings to create_db_engine. The lifespan runs create_all, then ensure_links_expires_at, then log_engine_tuning, and disposes the engine on shutdown. The router order stays health, links, redirect.

components.name: Documentation
components.responsibility: README, docs/API.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md (campaign deployment and scaling sections) and CHANGELOG [Unreleased], all accurate to the code.

api_contract.summary: Create a short link. Requires X-API-Key. Optional Idempotency-Key header and optional expires_at.
api_contract.request:
Headers:
- X-API-Key (required)
- Idempotency-Key (optional, 1-255 chars, not blank)

JSON body LinkCreate:
- url: string (strict http/https validation as today)
- expires_at: ISO 8601 datetime string or null (optional)

Offset values are converted to UTC, naive values are treated as UTC, and the value is stored as naive UTC. It must be strictly after the server's current time (checked in the service; the check is skipped on idempotent replay).

Response body LinkCreatedResponse: {code, short_url, url, is_active, created_at (UTC, 'Z'), expires_at (UTC 'Z' or null)}.

Response headers:
- Location: /api/links/{code}
- Idempotent-Replayed: true, on replay only

responses.201: Created, or idempotent replay (with Idempotent-Replayed: true); body LinkCreatedResponse including expires_at
responses.401: Invalid or missing API key (WWW-Authenticate: ApiKey)
responses.409: Idempotency-Key already used with a different payload (different url, or added/different/removed expires_at)
responses.422: Invalid body or URL, expires_at not a datetime string, or expires_at at or before now ({"detail": "expires_at must be in the future"})
responses.503: Short code allocation exhausted or database unavailable

api_contract.summary: Get link metadata, including deactivated and expired links. Requires X-API-Key.
api_contract.request:
Path code. Response body LinkDetailResponse:
- code, short_url, url, is_active
- created_at, deactivated_at: UTC 'Z' or null
- expires_at: UTC 'Z' or null
- is_expired: bool, true iff expires_at is not null and now >= expires_at
- total_clicks: int

responses.404: Link not found (unknown or malformed code)

api_contract.summary: Set, change or clear the expiry of an existing link. Requires X-API-Key.
api_contract.request:
JSON body LinkExpiryUpdate (extra fields forbidden): {"expires_at": <ISO 8601 datetime string> | null}. The field is required but may be null.
- A non-null value is normalised to naive UTC and must be strictly after now.
- null clears the expiry.
- The link is never reactivated.
- url, code, is_active, created_at, deactivated_at and idempotency records are untouched.

responses.404: Link not found (unknown or malformed code)
responses.422: Missing expires_at, unknown extra fields, non-datetime value, or expires_at at or before now; stored value unchanged

api_contract.summary: Deactivate (soft-delete) a link. Idempotent. Requires X-API-Key. Unchanged.
Daily click stats. Contract unchanged; now aggregated in SQL. Requires X-API-Key.
api_contract.request: Query days: int, 1..365, default 30. Response body LinkStatsResponse (unchanged): {code, total_clicks, clicks_per_day: [{date, count}], top_referrers: [{referrer, count}]}.

responses.200: LinkStatsResponse (unchanged shape and semantics; works for deactivated and expired links)

api_contract.summary: Clicks per UTC hour for one link over [start, end), zero-filled. Requires X-API-Key.
api_contract.request:
Query parameters (optional ISO 8601 datetimes): start and end. Offsets are converted to UTC and naive values are treated as UTC. Clients must URL-encode '+' as %2B.

Range rules:
- Both omitted: start = current UTC hour - 24h, end = current UTC hour + 1h (25 buckets).
- start is floored to the top of its hour; end is rounded up to the next top of hour (unchanged if already aligned).

Response body LinkHourlyStatsResponse: {code, start (UTC 'Z'), end (UTC 'Z'), total_clicks (sum over the range), clicks_per_hour: [{hour (UTC 'Z', top of hour), count}]}. Every hour in [start, end) is listed ascending; hours without clicks have count 0.

responses.200: LinkHourlyStatsResponse (works for active, deactivated and expired links)
responses.404: Link not found (unknown or malformed code)
responses.422: Only one of start/end supplied, aligned start >= aligned end, range longer than 744 hours, unparseable or out-of-range datetime

api_contract.summary: Public redirect. Records exactly one click on success (best-effort). The HEAD /{code} twin (not in the schema) returns the same status and headers and records no click.
api_contract.request:
Path code, which must match ^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,32}$ or the response is 404 with no SQL. Optional Referer and User-Agent headers are stored, truncated to 2048 and 512 characters. Order of checks:
1. Not found: 404.
2. Deactivated: 410 'Link has been deactivated'.
3. Expired (now >= expires_at): 410 'Link has expired'.
4. Otherwise: 307.

responses.307: Redirect; Location byte-identical to the stored URL; Cache-Control: no-store; empty body
responses.404: {"detail": "Link not found"}, Cache-Control: no-store, no Location
responses.410: {"detail": "Link has been deactivated"} (takes precedence) or {"detail": "Link has expired"}; Cache-Control: no-store; no Location; no click recorded
responses.503: {"detail": "Service temporarily unavailable"} when the link lookup itself fails (DB unavailable); no internal details

api_contract.summary: Liveness probe; never touches the DB. HEAD /healthz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body. POST returns 405.
Readiness probe (SELECT 1). HEAD /readyz (not in the schema) returns 200 with an empty body, or 503. POST returns 405.

responses.503: {"detail": "Database is not ready"} or the generic 503 detail; no exception text, SQL or stack trace

fields.name: code
fields.constraints: NOT NULL; UNIQUE uq_links_code. On SQLite and PostgreSQL the DDL is unchanged (VARCHAR(32)). On fresh MySQL databases it is COLLATE utf8mb4_bin. Existing MySQL databases need the manual ALTER (documented).

fields.name: expires_at
fields.constraints: NEW. Nullable, no default; NULL = never expires. Added to existing DBs by the idempotent startup upgrade: 'ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME' (PostgreSQL: 'ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE'). No index (never used in a WHERE clause).

data_model.name: ClickEvent (table click_events), unchanged

fields.name: ip_hash
fields.constraints: nullable; HMAC-SHA256 only when IP_HASH_SALT is set; no raw IP column

indexes: ix_click_events_link_id_created_at (link_id, created_at). Serves the daily and hourly half-open range aggregation as a covering index.

fields.name: request_hash
fields.constraints:
Semantics:
- expires_at absent: sha256(url) hex, the same as before the deploy, so old keys replay.
- expires_at present: sha256(url + '\n' + expires_at_naive_utc.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ')) hex.

Always 64 hex characters.

decisions.title: Harden SQLite with a connect listener, connect_args timeout and QueuePool settings
decisions.decision:
For file-based SQLite:
- create_engine(url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000.0}).
- An event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') handler executes the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a raw DBAPI cursor.
- The +0.5 ms makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation land exactly on the configured value.

In-memory SQLite gets only check_same_thread=False. Non-SQLite gets pool_pre_ping=True plus the pool settings.
decisions.rationale: WAL lets readers proceed while a writer holds the lock, which is what stops redirects queueing behind creates and clicks. The sqlite3 timeout parameter installs the busy handler without building a PRAGMA string, so the literal-only SQL policy holds. QueuePool kwargs are not valid for SingletonThreadPool/StaticPool, so in-memory URLs skip them.
alternatives: PRAGMA busy_timeout=<n> built with formatting (violates policy)
Move to PostgreSQL now (rejected by Q-2; needs a driver)
Leave the rollback journal and only add a busy timeout (readers would still block)

decisions.title: Idempotent startup ALTER instead of migration tooling
decisions.decision:
After create_all, the lifespan calls app.core.schema.ensure_links_expires_at(engine):
- It uses sqlalchemy.inspect on a fresh connection.
- If 'expires_at' is not among the links columns, it runs the dialect-guarded literal ALTER inside engine.begin().
- It logs 'added' or 'already_present'.
- On any exception it logs an ERROR and re-raises, so startup aborts.
decisions.rationale: There is one additive, nullable column and a one-week deadline. Alembic would add a dependency, a workflow and operator steps. Without the upgrade, every redirect on the deployed DB would return 503. Failing startup loudly is better than serving 503s.
alternatives: Alembic migrations (out of scope)
Documented manual ALTER only (operator error risk RK-11)
A separate link_expiry table (more joins on the hot path)

decisions.title: Expiry evaluated in Python on the narrow lookup row, with an injectable clock
decisions.decision: LinkRepository.get_redirect_target selects only id, url, is_active and expires_at. LinkService._check_redirectable(target) raises GoneError() if the link is inactive, then GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL) if expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= expires_at. GET and HEAD both go through _resolve_target, which calls _check_redirectable. The clock is LinkService(now=callable|None); _utcnow() calls it, falling back to models.utcnow(), and normalises to naive UTC.
decisions.rationale: This adds no SQL statements (FR-17). The rule is evaluated on every request with no cache (FR-22), and both methods share one helper (RK-14). Deactivation takes precedence. Tests are deterministic.
alternatives: WHERE expires_at > :now in SQL (cannot distinguish 404, 410-deactivated and 410-expired without a second query)
In-process cache of links (forbidden; breaks immediate deactivation and expiry)

decisions.title: Backward-compatible idempotency hash
decisions.decision: request_hash = sha256(url) when expires_at is None; otherwise sha256(url + '\n' + canonical UTC instant 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'). The replay check runs before the future-instant check.
decisions.rationale: Keys stored before the deploy (url-only hashes) keep replaying. The same instant written with different offsets hashes identically. Adding or changing expires_at gives 409. Replays return the stored link even after the expiry has passed, which matches how deactivated links replay.
alternatives: Always hash a JSON payload (breaks old keys, RK-15)
Ignore expires_at in the hash (silent replay of a different payload)

decisions.title: SQL aggregation with dialect-guarded bucket expressions that use no bound parameters
decisions.decision:
Daily and hourly stats use SELECT bucket, COUNT(id) ... WHERE link_id = :id AND created_at >= :start [AND created_at < :end] GROUP BY bucket.

Day bucket:
- sqlite: func.date(created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): cast(created_at, Date)
- mysql/mariadb: func.date(created_at)

Hour bucket:
- sqlite: func.strftime(literal_column("'%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00'"), created_at)
- postgresql (and the fallback): func.date_trunc(literal_column("'hour'"), created_at)
- mysql/mariadb: func.timestampadd(literal_column('HOUR'), func.hour(created_at), func.date(created_at))

Result values are normalised in Python (str -> date/datetime). Module-level statement builders take dialect_name so tests can compile them for all three dialects.
decisions.rationale: Memory is O(days) or O(hours) and the query uses the covering (link_id, created_at) index. With no bind parameters inside the bucket expression, the GROUP BY matches the SELECT expression on PostgreSQL. String formats are constants, not SQL formatting.
alternatives: Stream timestamps with yield_per and bucket in Python (portable but O(clicks) time)
Denormalised hourly counter table (new schema, out of scope)

decisions.title: Explicit HEAD routes for the probes
decisions.decision: health.py adds @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False). They return Response(status_code=200) with an empty body. /readyz shares a private _check_database(db) helper with GET.
decisions.rationale: This guarantees an empty body and leaves the OpenAPI path and operation set untouched. The health router is included before the catch-all, so HEAD /{code} never sees these paths. POST still yields 405.
alternatives: api_route(methods=['GET','HEAD']) (adds 'head' operations to the OpenAPI schema and relies on the server to strip the body)

decisions.title: End the read transaction before the click insert; best-effort WARNING on failure
decisions.decision:
In resolve_and_record_click, after the lookup and checks, call self.session.rollback(). This ends the read transaction and is a transaction-boundary call, not a statement. Then call ClickRepository.add(...) and session.commit() inside try/except Exception. On failure:
- Roll back, suppressing any secondary exception.
- Log exactly one logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)', link_id, type(exc).__name__), with no IP, no exception message and no traceback.
- Return the URL.
decisions.rationale: This avoids SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT on the read-to-write upgrade under WAL and bounds the added latency to the busy timeout. The exception message can contain bound SQL parameters, so it is not logged. ClickRepository.add remains the patch point used by existing tests.
alternatives: session.commit() after the read (shows up as a second COMMIT in the query budget)
BEGIN IMMEDIATE for the whole redirect (serialises reads behind writers)
Asynchronous click ingestion (out of scope, Q-5)

decisions.title: Future-instant validation in the service with a 422 domain error
decisions.decision: Add InvalidInputError(AppError) with status 422 in app/core/errors.py. Schemas only parse and normalise (to naive UTC, non-string values rejected). LinkService raises InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future') using its injectable clock. StatsService raises InvalidInputError for invalid hourly ranges.
decisions.rationale: Validation that depends on the clock must use the injectable clock and must be skipped on idempotent replay. A Pydantic validator cannot do either. The error body stays {"detail": "..."}.
alternatives: Pydantic validator calling datetime.now() (cannot be tested deterministically; would break replay)
Raise HTTPException from the services (violates layering)

decisions.title: No-store on redirect-path error responses
decisions.decision: redirect.py catches NotFoundError and GoneError from the service and returns JSONResponse({'detail': exc.detail}, status_code=exc.status_code, headers={'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}). Other exceptions propagate to the global handlers (SQLAlchemyError -> 503).
decisions.rationale: Browsers and CDNs could otherwise cache a 410 or 404 after a link is created, cleared or extended. Expiry and PATCH changes take effect immediately (NFR-15).
alternatives: Add no-store to every AppError in the global handler (wider blast radius)

decisions.title: MySQL case-sensitive codes via a type variant
decisions.decision: Declare code as String(32).with_variant(String(32, collation='utf8mb4_bin'), 'mysql', 'mariadb'). Document the manual DDL for existing MySQL databases: ALTER TABLE links MODIFY code VARCHAR(32) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin NOT NULL;
decisions.rationale: This keeps portable sqltypes (type(col.type) is still sqltypes.String) and leaves the SQLite and PostgreSQL DDL unchanged.
alternatives: A global collation (breaks SQLite)
Dialect-specific types from sqlalchemy.dialects (forbidden in models)

risks.description: The startup upgrade is not applied or is wrong, so every links query fails on the production DB (503 on every redirect).
risks.mitigation: Idempotent ensure_links_expires_at in the lifespan, which fails startup on error. Test against an old-schema SQLite file with existing rows and idempotency keys. Back up before deploying (runbook). Document the manual SQL.

risks.description: Pool kwargs passed for in-memory SQLite raise at create_app('sqlite://').
risks.mitigation: The in-memory branch passes only check_same_thread. Tests cover 'sqlite://' and ':memory:'.

risks.description: SQL bucketing differs from the old Python bucketing (window edges, ordering, return types).
risks.mitigation: Keep the >= since predicate and sort in Python. Normalise str to date/datetime. The unmodified tests/test_stats.py is the oracle, plus hourly boundary tests and compile tests for three dialects.

risks.description: A naive vs aware comparison, or datetime overflow (year 9999 with an offset, +1 hour at datetime.max), raises a 500.
risks.mitigation: Everything is normalised to naive UTC at the schema and service boundaries. OverflowError is converted to ValueError (schemas) or InvalidInputError (services). Tests use +01:00, -05:00 and +05:30 and extreme values.

risks.description: '+' in hourly query strings decodes as a space, so the offset is misread and the request returns 422.
risks.mitigation: Document URL-encoding (%2B) or using 'Z' in API.md and the runbook. A parse failure is a clean 422, never a wrong answer.

risks.description: Click drops under bursts because of the short busy timeout recommended for the campaign.
risks.mitigation: Every drop logs one WARNING (countable per hour). Default 5000 ms, runbook value 1000 ms. NFR-19 burst test.

risks.description: Operators enter the wrong expiry instant or year, or miss campaign links.
risks.mitigation: Runbook PATCH loop over the code list, verified with GET detail (expires_at, is_expired), as a pre-launch checklist item. PATCH allows correction.

risks.description: The WAL sidecar files break naive backups or network filesystems.
risks.mitigation: OPERATIONS.md: use sqlite3 .backup or copy all three files while the service is stopped; local writable directory only. The startup line shows the effective journal_mode.

risks.description: Overlapping concurrent work packages edit shared files.
risks.mitigation: Strict per-file ownership. Interfaces (names and signatures) are fixed in this design.

work_packages.title: Foundation: settings, engine hardening, schema upgrade, errors, logging fields, model column
work_packages.description:
No new requirements.txt entries. Core must not import app.api, app.services or app.repositories. Never use the identifier 'cache' or 'lru_cache'. text()/exec_driver_sql may only receive literal strings.

1) app/core/config.py: add fields to Settings and update the module docstring to list the new env names.
- sqlite_busy_timeout_ms: int = Field(5000, ge=0, le=60000)
- db_pool_size: int = Field(5, ge=1)
- db_max_overflow: int = Field(10, ge=0)
- db_pool_timeout_seconds: float = Field(30.0, gt=0, le=300)
Keep all existing fields, defaults and validators unchanged.

2) app/core/db.py:
- Add `def is_memory_sqlite(url: URL) -> bool`: true when url.get_backend_name() == 'sqlite' and (url.database in (None, '', ':memory:') or url.database.startswith('file::memory:') or url.query.get('mode') == 'memory').
- Change the signature to `create_db_engine(database_url: str, *, pool_size: int = 5, max_overflow: int = 10, pool_timeout: float = 30.0, sqlite_busy_timeout_ms: int = 5000) -> Engine`. Use make_url(database_url) and call `create_engine` through the module-level imported name (tests monkeypatch app.core.db.create_engine).
  (a) In-memory SQLite: create_engine(database_url, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False}). No pool kwargs, no listener.
  (b) File SQLite: create_engine(database_url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size=pool_size, max_overflow=max_overflow, pool_timeout=pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (sqlite_busy_timeout_ms + 0.5) / 1000.0}). Comment that the +0.5 makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation exact. Then register `@event.listens_for(engine, 'connect')` def _sqlite_on_connect(dbapi_connection, _record): cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor(); try: cursor.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL'); cursor.execute('PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL'); finally: cursor.close(). Use only literal strings and do not swallow errors. Do NOT enable foreign_keys.
  (c) Otherwise: create_engine(database_url, pool_pre_ping=True, pool_size=..., max_overflow=..., pool_timeout=...).
- Add `def describe_engine(engine: Engine) -> dict[str, object]`, returning {'dialect': engine.dialect.name, 'pool_class': type(engine.pool).__name__, 'pool_size': ..., 'max_overflow': ..., 'pool_timeout': ...}.
  - For a QueuePool, use pool.size(), pool._max_overflow and pool.timeout(). Otherwise all three are None.
  - For dialect 'sqlite', also open `with engine.connect() as conn:` and read journal_mode = conn.exec_driver_sql('PRAGMA journal_mode').scalar(), synchronous = ...('PRAGMA synchronous').scalar() and busy_timeout_ms = ...('PRAGMA busy_timeout').scalar().
  - Never include the URL.
- Add `def log_engine_tuning(engine: Engine) -> dict[str, object]`: info = describe_engine(engine); then logging.getLogger('app.db').info('database tuning ' + ' '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k, v in info.items()), extra=info); return info. Building the log message with formatting is fine because it is not SQL.
- create_session_factory and get_db are unchanged.

3) NEW app/core/schema.py:
- `logger = logging.getLogger('app.db')`.
- `def ensure_links_expires_at(engine: Engine) -> bool` (True if the column was added):
  - with engine.connect() as conn: columns = {c['name'] for c in inspect(conn).get_columns('links')}.
  - If 'expires_at' is in columns: logger.info('schema upgrade: links.expires_at already present', extra={'schema_upgrade': 'already_present'}) and return False.
  - Otherwise, with engine.begin() as conn: if engine.dialect.name == 'postgresql': conn.exec_driver_sql('ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE'); else: conn.exec_driver_sql('ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME').
  - Then logger.info('schema upgrade: links.expires_at added', extra={'schema_upgrade': 'added'}) and return True.
  - Wrap the whole body in try/except Exception: logger.exception('schema upgrade failed: could not add links.expires_at'); raise.

4) app/core/errors.py:
- Add `LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL = 'Link has expired'`.
- Add `class InvalidInputError(AppError): status_code = 422; default_detail = 'Invalid input'`.
- Nothing else changes (the existing handlers already map AppError).

1) app/services/link_service.py

Imports: Callable from collections.abc; datetime; InvalidInputError and LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL from app.core.errors; to_naive_utc from app.models; RedirectTarget from app.repositories.

LinkDetail dataclass: add `is_expired: bool = False`.

__init__: add keyword `now: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None`, stored as self._clock.

`def _utcnow(self) -> datetime`: value = self._clock() if self._clock is not None else utcnow(); return to_naive_utc(value). Resolve the module-level utcnow at call time so monkeypatching app.services.link_service.utcnow works.

`def _is_expired(self, expires_at: datetime | None) -> bool`: return expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= to_naive_utc(expires_at).

`def _check_redirectable(self, target: RedirectTarget) -> None`: if not target.is_active: raise GoneError(); if self._is_expired(target.expires_at): raise GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL).

`def _resolve_target(self, code: str) -> RedirectTarget`:
- If not codes.is_valid_code_format(code): raise NotFoundError() (no SQL).
- target = self.link_repo.get_redirect_target(code); None -> NotFoundError().
- self._check_redirectable(target); return target.

resolve_for_redirect(code) -> str: return self._resolve_target(code).url.

resolve_and_record_click(code, referrer, user_agent, client_ip) -> str:
- target = self._resolve_target(code).
- self.session.rollback() to end the read transaction before the write (comment: avoids SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT; this is a transaction boundary, not a statement).
- try: self.click_repo.add(ClickEvent(link_id=target.id, referrer=..., user_agent=..., ip_hash=hash_ip(client_ip, self.ip_hash_salt))) with the same truncation as today; self.session.commit().
- except Exception as exc: try: self.session.rollback() except Exception: pass; then logger.warning('failed to record click for link_id=%s (%s)', target.id, type(exc).__name__). This is the only log call: no exc_info, no message text, no IP.
- return target.url.

create_link(self, url: str, idempotency_key: str | None = None, expires_at: datetime | None = None) -> CreateResult:
- Validate the key as today.
- expires_at = to_naive_utc(expires_at) if not None.
- request_hash = self._request_hash(url, expires_at).
- Replay or conflict check as today, BEFORE any future check.
- Then: if expires_at is not None and expires_at <= self._utcnow(): raise InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future').
- Generation loop as today, with Link(code=code, url=url, is_active=True, expires_at=expires_at).

`@staticmethod def _request_hash(url, expires_at) -> str`:
- None -> hashlib.sha256(url.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() (unchanged).
- Otherwise sha256((url + '\n' + expires_at.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ')).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest().

get_link_detail(code): link = self._get_or_404(code); return LinkDetail(link=link, total_clicks=..., is_expired=self._is_expired(link.expires_at)). Keep the signature (self, code); tests monkeypatch it.

NEW `def set_expiry(self, code: str, expires_at: datetime | None) -> LinkDetail`:
- link = self._get_or_404(code) (404 first).
- If expires_at is not None: expires_at = to_naive_utc(expires_at); if expires_at <= self._utcnow(): raise InvalidInputError('expires_at must be in the future').
- link.expires_at = expires_at; self.session.commit(); return self.get_link_detail(code).
- Never touch is_active, deactivated_at, url, code or idempotency rows.

deactivate: use self._utcnow() instead of utcnow().

Update the module docstring.

2) app/services/stats_service.py

- MAX_HOURLY_RANGE_HOURS = 744; DEFAULT_HOURLY_LOOKBACK_HOURS = 24.
- Add `@dataclass class HourlyStats: code: str; start: datetime; end: datetime; total_clicks: int; clicks_per_hour: list[tuple[datetime, int]]`.
- get_stats: same signature and semantics, but replace the Counter over created_at_since with clicks_per_day = self.click_repo.daily_counts(link.id, since) (already a sorted list of (date, int)). Remove the Counter import if unused. The total and referrers are unchanged. Update the module docstring (SQL aggregation).
- NEW `def get_hourly_clicks(self, code: str, start: datetime | None = None, end: datetime | None = None, now: datetime | None = None) -> HourlyStats`:
  (a) If exactly one of start/end is None: raise InvalidInputError('start and end must be supplied together').
  (b) Normalise: try: start/end = to_naive_utc(...), now = to_naive_utc(now) or utcnow(); except OverflowError: raise InvalidInputError('datetime out of range').
  (c) If both are None: cur = now with minute/second/microsecond set to 0; start = cur - timedelta(hours=24); end = cur + timedelta(hours=1).
      Else: start = floor_hour(start); end_floor = floor_hour(end); end = end_floor if end_floor == end else end_floor + 1h. Wrap the arithmetic in try/except OverflowError -> InvalidInputError.
  (d) If start >= end: raise InvalidInputError('start must be before end').
  (e) hours = int((end - start).total_seconds() // 3600); if hours > 744: raise InvalidInputError('range must not exceed 744 hours').
  (f) Then the code check: invalid format or link missing -> NotFoundError(). Works for inactive and expired links.
  (g) counts = dict(self.click_repo.hourly_counts(link.id, start, end)); buckets = [(start + timedelta(hours=i), counts.get(start + timedelta(hours=i), 0)) for i in range(hours)]; total = sum(c for _, c in buckets).
  (h) Return HourlyStats(link.code, start, end, total, buckets).
  Import InvalidInputError from app.core.errors and to_naive_utc from app.models.
